task_description:
The Capacitor iOS app sometimes loads stale UI instead of the latest dev server build.

Investigate and fix the caching behavior so the app always loads the most recent code during development. Add a visible build identifier so we can instantly verify which build is running.

Scope

Development mode only (do not affect production behavior)

Minimal, surgical changes

Must be verifiable visually and in logs

Acceptance Criteria

On iOS dev builds, the app reliably loads the latest code after restart

A visible build stamp is shown (timestamp or commit hash), e.g.:

Settings screen or

Small footer/corner overlay

Build stamp updates when code changes

No regressions in Android or web

Likely Areas

capacitor.config.ts

ios/App/AppDelegate.swift

ios/App/Info.plist

Any WebView cache configuration

Frontend Settings UI

Deliverables

Code changes committed

Brief explanation of why the caching happened

Screenshot showing updated build stamp
Why this is the right first task

This task is:

Bounded (one problem, one platform)

Observable (you can see success immediately)

Trust-building (Auto-Claude proves it can touch native + frontend safely)

Unblocks everything else (no more “is this the old build?” anxiety)

It’s also psychologically important:
you move from tool setup → felt reliability.

What to do immediately after creating it

Create the task

Do nothing for 30–60 seconds

Watch Auto-Claude move it:

Planning → In Progress → AI Review

If it asks a clarification question, paste it here and I’ll answer in a way that keeps it on rails.

What comes next (don’t do yet)

After this lands cleanly, the second task should be:

“Add voice capture to Quick Journal (local storage only)”

But don’t queue that yet.
One successful task builds momentum and calibrates the agent.

Go ahead — create the task.
When it moves to In Progress, send a screenshot or paste the first planning note it generates, and we’ll tune it together.
